tasks.short: Improve how we select, grade, reward and develop people across our three sites.

today.trigger: A manager requests a change, recruitment becomes difficult, or an approved CAO change affects existing methods.
steps: Gather existing policies, applicable CAO provisions and examples from managers.
Compare selection, progression and reward practices across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
Draft revised criteria and calculate example outcomes in Excel.
Review proposals with HR Business Partners, Payroll and the HR Director, involving the OR where required.
Explain approved changes to managers and check their application.
drudgery: Finding the latest policy and CAO versions
today.time_sinks: Reconciling local practices and collecting examples usually takes longer than writing the proposal.

lenses.faster: Assemble the relevant approved clauses and calculate standard examples automatically. AI drafts a comparison of current practice and proposed changes for me to check.
lenses.autonomous: An approved policy change or a scheduled review starts an evidence pack and requests missing inputs. Changes to selection, promotion or pay methods still require human decisions.
lenses.ambitious: Test proposed methods against ten times more representative job and shift situations before rollout. Follow whether clearer progression and offers support productive hires who stay beyond day 90.
lenses.joy: Remove document hunting and repeated spreadsheet preparation. Keep the work of resolving unfair inconsistencies and helping managers explain decisions.
lenses.options: Compare five approaches, such as clearer entry grades, skill progression or revised allowances, with cost and implementation consequences.
lenses.altitude: I become the owner of the rules, examples and review process used to maintain consistent reward and progression methods.
reach: Help Recruiters prepare consistent offer guidance.
Help L&D connect approved skill milestones to progression.
Help the Controller assess the cost of policy alternatives.

tasks.human_edge: Judging fairness, understanding actual warehouse work and negotiating acceptable changes with managers and employee representatives.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: AI can assemble evidence and draft alternatives, while people must choose methods that affect employment opportunities and rewards.

in_practice.trigger: The specialist opens a policy review or records a verified CAO change in a controlled SharePoint register.
steps: Retrieve approved policy versions and aggregate job, pay and recruitment figures.
Run deterministic cost examples using the correct CAO, grade and effective date.
Draft alternative methods with clause references, assumptions and unresolved questions.
Review outcomes with HR, Payroll and managers and complete the applicable OR process.
Publish approved guidance and schedule a check of exceptions and hiring outcomes.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist validates the analysis; the HR Director approves policy changes, with Payroll validation and OR involvement where applicable.
systems: AFAS Profit read-only export or configured GetConnector
data_needed: Verified CAO scope and effective-dated provisions
Approved job families, grades and progression rules
Manager examples with unnecessary personal details removed
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint policy register containing source versions, calculations, decisions and approvals.

evidence.claim: Evidence assembly and drafting are plausible uses; the 25% saving is an unmeasured estimate for Noordhaven.
Changes to remuneration systems can require OR consent; individual pay amounts are a separate matter.
AI intended for employment decisions needs an EU AI Act classification assessment; human review alone does not determine its classification.

risks: Applying the transport CAO to a warehouse role, or using a provision outside its effective period.
Treating correlation between reward and retention as proof of causation.
Allowing drafting support to become unassessed employee ranking or automated promotion recommendations.
Implementing a system change before completing the applicable OR process.
research_questions: Which parts of this work does the specialist own, and which belong to HR Business Partners or L&D?
Can each job be reliably mapped to its applicable CAO and approved grade?
Does a pilot reduce preparation time without increasing correction or consultation time?
Can productive-at-day-90 outcomes be defined consistently enough to evaluate changes?

tasks.short: Maintain fair appraisal and employment practices, and work through changes with managers and the OR.

today.trigger: An appraisal review, employee concern or management request exposes a problem with an employment programme.
steps: Collect programme documents, aggregate outcomes and concerns raised by employees or managers.
Compare how the programme operates across sites and shifts.
Develop changes to appraisal guidance, access to development or employment equity practices.
Discuss proposals with HR Business Partners, the HR Director and the OR as applicable.
Support implementation and evaluate complaints, participation and consistency.
drudgery: Combining programme feedback from separate documents
today.time_sinks: Consultation, conflicting interests and inconsistent appraisal records dominate elapsed time.

lenses.faster: AI groups de-identified feedback and drafts programme changes and consultation packs. Fixed calculations compare participation and outcomes across sufficiently large groups.
lenses.autonomous: Scheduled programme reviews generate aggregate indicators and request updates from action owners. Sensitive complaints and labour relations discussions stay with people.
lenses.ambitious: Review access to appraisal, progression and development across every site and shift, including relevant agency-worker interfaces. Use small pilots to establish whether changes improve perceived fairness.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated pack preparation and action chasing. Keep listening, mediation and the work of making agreements that people trust.
lenses.options: Prepare several appraisal formats and rollout approaches, showing the burden on shift managers and how employees can question outcomes.
lenses.altitude: I design how programme fairness is checked and how concerns lead to documented improvements.
reach: Prepare programme evaluation evidence for HR Business Partners.
Support the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst with definitions for fairness indicators.
Help L&D identify unequal access to development.

tasks.human_edge: Employees need someone who understands their concerns, can challenge management and can negotiate without treating every issue as a data problem.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: programme design benefits from synthesis and drafting, but legitimacy depends on human consultation, context and accountability.

in_practice.trigger: An approved review date arrives or an HR Business Partner commissions a programme review.
steps: Build a restricted evidence pack from approved aggregate data and de-identified themes.
Calculate participation and outcome differences, flagging small samples and missing records.
Draft programme alternatives and a consultation agenda without individual employee scores.
Hold employee and manager discussions and complete the applicable OR process.
Record the approved programme, owners and follow-up measures.
in_practice.human_gate: HR Business Partners validate context, the specialist checks analysis, and the HR Director approves changes after required consultation.
data_needed: Lawfully available comparison variables and agreed disclosure thresholds
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint programme register; identifiable complaints remain in their separately controlled case records.

evidence.claim: Feedback synthesis and consultation drafting could reduce preparation effort; the proposed saving has not been measured.
OR consent rights cover specified personnel arrangements, including remuneration and job evaluation systems.
Processing personal data through AI requires attention to lawful basis, transparency and security.

risks: Importing US affirmative-action practices without checking Dutch equal-treatment requirements.
Inferring protected characteristics or collecting sensitive data without a valid basis.
Identifying employees through small shift or job groups.
AI summaries removing minority concerns or presenting contested claims as facts.
research_questions: Which programme outcomes are recorded consistently across the three sites?
Can feedback be de-identified without losing the context needed to understand it?
Which comparisons can lawfully and meaningfully be made with existing data?
Do employees and the OR find the proposed evaluation process credible?

tasks.short: Keep reward records and the employee handbook accurate when policies or employment terms change.

today.trigger: An approved employment change, corrected record or verified CAO update requires records or handbook text to change.
steps: Check the approved request and identify affected AFAS fields or handbook sections.
Compare existing records and text with the authoritative source.
Prepare record corrections and revise handbook wording.
Obtain approval from the responsible HR or Payroll owner.
Update the approved record or handbook and notify affected users.
drudgery: Copying approved values between documents and records
Finding every occurrence of an outdated rule
today.time_sinks: Checking effective dates, resolving inconsistent source documents and verifying that the correct version was published.

lenses.faster: Generate record-change proposals and handbook redlines from approved source changes. Field validation and document comparisons replace repeated manual checking.
lenses.autonomous: An approved change starts validation, drafting and an approval request. Publication and permitted record updates execute after approval.
lenses.ambitious: Check the whole handbook for contradictions whenever a rule changes, and provide plain-language explanations for warehouse and office staff.
lenses.joy: Remove rekeying, version naming and repetitive proofreading. Keep resolving ambiguous rules and answering questions that affect employees.
lenses.options: Produce concise, detailed and shift-friendly versions of the same approved explanation, with all versions tied to one source.
lenses.altitude: I own the source hierarchy, validation rules and publication controls that keep reward information dependable.
reach: Take routine reward-related document maintenance from HR Administrators.
Prepare validated record corrections for Payroll.
Help the HRIS Analyst define checks for incomplete reward records.

tasks.human_edge: Interpreting ambiguous employment terms and recognising when a seemingly clerical correction could change someone's entitlement.
tasks.pattern_why: agent_with_gate: deterministic checks handle fields and versions, an llm_step drafts text, and an accountable person approves each change package.

in_practice.trigger: An authorised change request reaches an approved status in the controlled workflow.
steps: Read the approved source, employee or policy identifier, scope and effective date.
Validate structured changes and generate handbook redlines with source references.
Route the exact proposed values and document version to the responsible approver.
Apply approved changes through supported AFAS interfaces or an administrator, and publish approved text.
Read back changed values, verify publication and record completion or exceptions.
in_practice.human_gate: HR or Payroll approves the exact change package; substantive policy interpretation receives specialist review before any update.
systems: AFAS Profit configured connectors or controlled import
data_needed: Field mappings, effective-date rules and supported update interfaces
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS change history where available and a restricted SharePoint register of sources, before-and-after values, approvals and verification.

evidence.claim: AFAS provides GetConnectors for retrieval and UpdateConnectors for supported record changes; exact field coverage must be checked.
SharePoint document approval can be automated with Power Automate.
The combined record-and-handbook workflow and its 60% saving are proposed, not demonstrated at Noordhaven.

risks: A wrong employee identifier or effective date changing an entitlement.
AI rewriting a clause in a way that changes its meaning.
A retry applying the same change twice or overwriting a later correction.
Personnel documents becoming visible through incorrect SharePoint permissions.
research_questions: Which reward fields can the configured AFAS interfaces safely read and update?
How much of the 42.7 hours concerns routine records versus substantive handbook interpretation?
Can approvals be bound to the exact document version and proposed field values?
Can the workflow detect duplicates and verify updates without overwriting later changes?

tasks.short: Produce job, grade, organisation and career-path reports from approved HR data.

today.trigger: Management requests a report or a job evaluation and reward review reaches its reporting stage.
steps: Extract approved job, reporting-line, grade and pay information.
Reconcile missing identifiers and inconsistent job titles.
Build tables, organisation charts and career-path diagrams.
Write findings and check figures against the source.
Review and distribute the report to its authorised audience.
drudgery: Rebuilding charts after small organisational changes
today.time_sinks: Cleaning job mappings and manually keeping charts, tables and narrative consistent.

lenses.faster: Use a validated data model to generate tables and diagrams from approved relationships. AI drafts commentary only from the resulting checked figures.
lenses.autonomous: A successful nightly refresh rebuilds internal reports and flags changes. New narrative and wider distribution wait for approval.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain usable career maps for every approved job family, including routes from warehouse entry roles to skilled and supervisory work.
lenses.joy: Remove chart redrawing and slide reconciliation. Keep explaining what the structure means and correcting misleading interpretations.
lenses.options: Generate views by site, job family, grade and progression route, with appropriate suppression of small groups.
lenses.altitude: I define the reporting model and checks, then focus on whether reports support clear and fair career decisions.
reach: Maintain standard reward reporting alongside the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst.
Provide approved career maps to Recruiters and L&D.
Prepare aggregate workforce structure views for the Controller.

tasks.human_edge: Distinguishing a reporting relationship from a realistic career route and explaining limitations before managers act on a chart.
tasks.pattern_why: deterministic_software: structured data, fixed calculations and repeatable chart generation produce most of the report; an optional llm_step drafts checked commentary.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly AFAS extract completes successfully or an authorised user requests a dated report.
steps: Validate freshness, row counts, job identifiers and reporting relationships.
Calculate approved measures and generate standard charts and career maps.
Suppress restricted details and show source dates and unresolved data exceptions.
Generate a draft summary from checked aggregates and route material changes for review.
Refresh approved internal views and distribute reviewed report versions.
in_practice.human_gate: Routine validated internal views refresh automatically; the specialist approves new commentary, changed career routes and external or wider distribution.
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted reporting register with extract timestamp, validation results, report version and publication decisions.

evidence.claim: Power BI supports scheduled refresh, subject to configuration and operational limits.
Generating charts from validated relationships is feasible; the complete reporting workflow and 65% saving remain estimates.

risks: Presenting the nightly extract as current live information.
Publishing named compensation or exposing individuals through small groups.
Inventing progression routes from job-title similarities.
Polished charts hiding missing positions or invalid reporting relationships.
research_questions: Does AFAS contain reliable position and reporting-line data, or only employee-level fields?
Which career routes have actually been approved by operations and L&D?
Can generated reports reconcile exactly to an agreed source snapshot?
What share of reporting effort is recurring formatting rather than one-off analysis?

tasks.short: Research how logistics jobs are changing and what skills, responsibilities and qualifications they require.

today.trigger: A new role, operational change or difficult vacancy requires an updated understanding of job requirements.
steps: Review existing job descriptions, vacancies and qualification requirements.
Interview managers and jobholders and observe representative work.
Research relevant occupational and logistics trends.
Compare findings with approved job families and grades.
Recommend changes and confirm them with operations, HR and L&D.
today.time_sinks: Separating real work requirements from outdated descriptions and arranging observations across shifts.

lenses.faster: AI extracts requirements from approved descriptions and sourced research into a comparison table. I spend less time reading duplicates and more time verifying gaps on the warehouse floor.
lenses.autonomous: A scheduled source check drafts a digest of changes affecting named job families. It does not change job requirements or employee grades.
lenses.ambitious: Keep evidence-based requirements current across all job families, including new automation-related work. Check whether unnecessary entry requirements are restricting recruitment.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive reading and note consolidation. Keep observing work and discovering routes that help people progress.
lenses.options: Compare hiring for an existing skill, training after entry, redesigning the work or creating a progression role.
lenses.altitude: I maintain an evidence-backed model of jobs and skills, with clear rules for when a role needs re-evaluation.
reach: Improve vacancy requirements with Recruiters.
Identify training gaps with L&D.
Provide job-change evidence for workforce planning.

tasks.human_edge: Seeing actual work, hearing overlooked jobholders and recognising safety, responsibility and workload that documents fail to capture.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: AI accelerates document research and comparison, while interviews, observation and interpretation remain essential.

in_practice.trigger: Operations or HR requests a job review, or a scheduled research digest identifies a potentially relevant change.
steps: Collect approved internal documents and dated, attributable external sources.
Extract tasks, skills, qualifications and relationships with links to supporting passages.
Mark conflicting, outdated and unsupported requirements for investigation.
Interview and observe representative jobholders across relevant sites and shifts.
Approve revised job evidence and send proposed requirement changes to the responsible owners.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist and operational job owner validate every material requirement; safety and certificate requirements need the relevant expert's confirmation.
systems: Approved enterprise LLM with source retrieval, proposed addition
data_needed: Current job descriptions and vacancy requirements
De-identified interview notes and observation findings
Dated occupational research and sector publications
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint job evidence library containing source dates, extracted claims, verification notes and approved revisions.

evidence.claim: Source-linked extraction and comparison are plausible support for job research; neither local accuracy nor the 40% saving has been demonstrated.

risks: Importing foreign occupational requirements that do not fit Dutch logistics work.
Treating vacancy wording as proof of an essential qualification.
Missing physical demands or safety responsibilities absent from documents.
Overrepresenting office staff and day shifts in research.
research_questions: How often do existing descriptions disagree with observed work?
Can extracted requirements be traced accurately to their sources?
Are jobholders from all relevant sites and shifts available for validation?
Does the research identify removable entry barriers without weakening safety requirements?

tasks.short: Create practical questionnaires and interview guides for analysing and evaluating our jobs.

today.trigger: A job evaluation project or a poorly understood role needs better evidence collection.
steps: Define what the job analysis must establish and which approved evaluation method applies.
Review existing questionnaires and missing evidence.
Draft questions, interview prompts and evidence examples.
Pilot the materials with representative jobholders and managers.
Revise the instrument and brief the people collecting evidence.
today.time_sinks: Removing ambiguous questions and ensuring warehouse workers can describe responsibilities in terms the evaluation method recognises.

lenses.faster: Generate first drafts from the approved evaluation framework and flag missing evidence areas. Consolidate pilot feedback into one revision list.
lenses.autonomous: An approved job-analysis brief produces a draft questionnaire and completeness check. The instrument remains unpublished until I validate it.
lenses.ambitious: Pilot instruments across different sites, shifts and language needs rather than relying on one manager's feedback.
lenses.joy: Remove formatting and repetitive question drafting. Keep designing questions that reveal the work people actually do.
lenses.options: Prepare a short interview guide, a self-completion questionnaire and an observation checklist that collect the same required evidence.
lenses.altitude: I manage a tested instrument library and improve its reliability instead of starting each questionnaire from scratch.
reach: Give HR Business Partners consistent job-interview materials.
Help Recruiters distinguish essential requirements from preferences.
Help L&D collect evidence of changing skill requirements.

tasks.human_edge: Choosing neutral questions, noticing when workers interpret them differently and protecting the integrity of the approved job evaluation method.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: drafting and coverage checks are tractable, but instrument validity and suitability require expert design and real-world pilots.

in_practice.trigger: The specialist approves a brief stating the job family, evidence gaps and evaluation framework.
steps: Retrieve authorised framework materials and previously validated questions.
Draft questions and map each to a required evidence area.
Check for leading wording, unnecessary personal questions and unsupported scoring logic.
Pilot with representative workers and compare how consistently the questions are understood.
Approve the revised version and issue interviewer guidance.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves every instrument after a pilot; changes to the underlying evaluation system receive the required separate approval process.
in_practice.logs_to: Versioned SharePoint instrument library with framework mapping, pilot findings, approval and retirement dates.

evidence.claim: AI-assisted question drafting and coverage mapping are plausible; reliable instruments still require human testing, and the saving is estimated.

risks: Accidentally changing the approved evaluation method through new questions or scoring.
Questions rewarding articulate descriptions rather than actual job demands.
Uploading licensed evaluation materials to an unapproved model.
Translated wording changing the meaning of responsibility or physical-demand questions.
research_questions: Which evaluation framework is approved, and does its licence permit this use?
Do different interviewers obtain comparable evidence with the proposed instrument?
Can shift workers complete it within a practical amount of paid work time?
Does a pilot find fewer ambiguous answers than the current questionnaire?

tasks.short: Analyse workforce and sector data to explain reward issues and support business decisions.

today.trigger: HR or Finance requests analysis, or an authorised external information request needs a response.
steps: Clarify the question, audience and permitted data scope.
Gather AFAS extracts, dashboard figures and relevant external benchmarks.
Reconcile definitions, periods and employee populations.
Analyse patterns and prepare a written explanation with limitations.
Review findings with HR or Finance and approve any external disclosure.
today.time_sinks: Making populations and pay measures comparable, especially across employees, agency workers and different shift patterns.

lenses.faster: Reusable calculations standardise populations and pay measures. AI drafts explanations from checked results and lists assumptions that need my judgment.
lenses.autonomous: A successful refresh runs agreed data checks and prepares recurring analysis. Unusual findings and external submissions are routed for review.
lenses.ambitious: Test reward and workforce questions by site, job family and shift regularly, using sufficiently large groups. Connect findings to hiring and day-90 outcomes without claiming causation.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated cleaning and copying. Keep investigating anomalies and helping managers understand the choices available.
lenses.options: Compare wage growth, allowances, training investment and agency-mix scenarios with explicit assumptions and sensitivity ranges.
lenses.altitude: I own the definitions and analytical questions that make reward evidence useful to management.
reach: Prepare reward-cost scenarios with FP&A.
Resolve workforce-cost definition differences with the Controller.
Develop repeatable reward measures with the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst.

tasks.human_edge: Choosing meaningful comparisons, challenging misleading benchmarks and explaining uncertainty before figures influence employment or budget decisions.
tasks.pattern_why: agent_with_gate: deterministic calculations and an llm_step can prepare an analysis pack, but interpretation and consequential disclosure require approval.

in_practice.trigger: An approved analytical request or recurring reporting date initiates a defined analysis.
steps: Load authorised snapshots and verify dates, definitions and population coverage.
Calculate approved measures, reconciling employee pay and agency invoice concepts separately.
Run sensitivity checks and suppress disclosive small-group results.
Draft a source-linked briefing containing findings, limitations and unresolved questions.
Obtain specialist and relevant Finance or HR approval before release.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves interpretation; the relevant data owner approves external disclosures and Finance validates financial conclusions.
data_needed: Approved metric definitions and population rules
Effective-dated pay, hours, grades and contract categories
Agency hours and invoice breakdowns where comparison requires them
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint analysis register with snapshot identifiers, calculation version, assumptions, approvals and recipients.

evidence.claim: AFAS supports configured retrieval of records through GetConnectors.
Repeatable calculations and checked narrative could reduce preparation time; the complete workflow and 45% saving are unmeasured.

risks: Comparing employee gross pay directly with agency invoice rates that include additional costs.
Ignoring FTE, shift allowances, tenure or benchmark reference dates.
Exposing personal pay or identifiable absence information.
An AI-written explanation overstating a correlation or concealing missing data.
research_questions: Can HR and Finance agree on headcount, FTE, hourly pay and total labour-cost definitions?
Are agency hours and invoice components sufficiently detailed for valid comparisons?
Which recurring analyses justify a maintained workflow at this task's annual volume?
Can every published number and conclusion be reproduced from a dated source snapshot?

tasks.short: Teach managers and employees how our pay, benefits and job-grading rules work.

today.trigger: An approved reward change, recurring misunderstanding or manager onboarding creates a training need.
steps: Agree the audience and learning goals with L&D and Payroll.
Gather approved policies and common questions.
Develop slides, examples, exercises and reference materials.
Deliver sessions at times that accommodate relevant shifts.
Collect feedback and revise unclear material.
drudgery: Creating similar exercises for each audience
Updating handouts after a rule changes
today.time_sinks: Preparing accurate examples and arranging sessions that warehouse and transport staff can attend.

lenses.faster: AI drafts a lesson plan, slides and exercises from approved policies. Fixed calculators produce examples that Payroll can verify once and reuse.
lenses.autonomous: An approved policy change flags affected learning materials and prepares revisions. L&D assigns approved learning through the available Studytube process.
lenses.ambitious: Offer short, shift-accessible explanations of payslips, allowances and progression, and check understanding before day 90.
lenses.joy: Remove slide production and repetitive handout updates. Keep live questions, practical demonstrations and helping employees understand their pay.
lenses.options: Create a manager workshop, a short employee module and a toolbox briefing from the same approved content.
lenses.altitude: I own reward-learning accuracy and evaluate whether learning reduces confusion and manager errors.
reach: Develop reward modules jointly with L&D.
Provide verified pay explanations for Payroll.
Supply consistent reward information for onboarding.

tasks.human_edge: Answering sensitive pay questions, noticing misunderstanding and explaining exceptions without exposing another employee's circumstances.
tasks.pattern_why: copilot: content preparation becomes faster, while teaching, discussion and confirmation of understanding remain human work.

in_practice.trigger: L&D commissions reward training or an approved policy change identifies affected materials.
steps: Retrieve the approved policy version and agree learning objectives and audiences.
Draft lessons, worked examples, exercises and accessible reference sheets.
Have the specialist and Payroll check every entitlement statement and calculation.
Pilot with representative learners, then publish through the agreed Studytube process and deliver live sessions.
Review comprehension and recurring questions and revise approved materials.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist and Payroll approve content accuracy; L&D approves learning design and publication, and qualified assessors retain any required certification decisions.
data_needed: Approved reward policies and effective dates
Permitted enrolment, completion and feedback data
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint learning-content register for sources and approvals; Studytube for actual enrolments and completions.

evidence.claim: Drafting policy-based lessons and exercises is plausible; the 30% saving assumes preparation improves while live teaching remains necessary.
Power Automate can route document approval before publication, if added and configured.

risks: Incorrect allowance examples spreading through multiple training formats.
Employees on shifts lacking paid time or practical access to online learning.
Translations changing the meaning of employment entitlements.
Treating module completion as proof of competence or automatically granting forklift, VCA or food-safety certificates.
research_questions: How much training preparation currently repeats approved material?
Which formats and languages can shift workers use during paid work time?
What content formats and assignment methods does Noordhaven's Studytube configuration support?
Does the pilot improve understanding and reduce repeat questions without increasing incorrect advice?

role.altitude: The specialist becomes the owner of reliable reward rules, job evidence and explanations, using repeatable workflows to support fair decisions across three sites.
reach: Maintain routine reward documents and validated correction packages with HR Administration and Payroll.
Provide approved offer and career-path guidance to Recruiters.
Co-own reward learning and skill-to-progression maps with L&D.
Develop workforce-cost scenarios with FP&A and the Controller.
Define reward data checks and measures with the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst.
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks total 335.1 hours a year, about 21% of a 1,600-hour role. The estimates imply roughly 140 hours released, worth about EUR 10,500 in gross capacity at EUR 75/hour, before implementation, licensing and maintenance; this is not a cash saving or a whole-role forecast. Current workflows are inferred from the company description. Savings assume steady-state operation, and speedups describe active task processing including review and automated execution; consultation and approval queues may leave calendar turnaround largely unchanged. Shared data and document workflows should be built with HRIS support rather than as eight separate systems. Employment decisions, negotiations, job observation and live teaching retain substantial human work. Clinical absence information and Wet verbetering poortwachter case decisions remain with the designated absence professionals.
skills_to_grow: Translate CAO and reward policies into effective-dated rules and test cases.
Design job evidence collection and evaluate instrument reliability.
Use Excel and Power BI to reconcile populations, costs and assumptions.
Specify AFAS access, validation, approval and read-back controls with HRIS.
Check AI drafts against authoritative sources and recognise unsupported conclusions.
Apply AVG/GDPR data minimisation, access controls and retention requirements.
Assess the intended use of employment AI under the EU AI Act with qualified support.
Consult the OR effectively and explain reward choices to shift workers.
role.ambitious_version: Give Noordhaven one maintained source for job requirements, grades, progression and reward explanations, with every change traceable to an approved decision. Use the released capacity to test whether clearer offers, realistic career routes and understandable pay improve acceptance and productive 90-day retention, while managers and HR retain responsibility for individual decisions.
